title: Extending interior point method to nonlinear programming using trust regions
contribution: Extends the LP primal barrier method to nonlinear programming by viewing affine scaling as an ellipsoidal trust region on QP subproblems with linearized equalities, keeping the log barrier for the bounds, reducing to the primal barrier method on LPs, and testing it with the Byrd-Omojokun equality-constrained trust-region code (abstract).
problem_entry: Extend the primal barrier interior-point method of LP to general nonlinear optimization (abstract).
key_idea: Recast affine scaling as an ellipsoidal trust region on iterative QP subproblems with linearized equalities; keep the log-barrier term for centring w.r.t. bounds; iterates interior to bounds, equalities satisfied only at convergence (abstract).
experiments: Test results obtained with the Lalee-Nocedal-Plantenga implementation of the Byrd-Omojokun algorithm; results not in the abstract (abstract).
positioning: Generalizes the LP primal barrier method; precedes S008/S009 (works.json note: probably a conference abstract, not verified).
limits_future: Not stated (abstract).

method_links.note: Engine half only: the existing Byrd-Omojokun equality-constrained trust-region code is reused; the new part is the barrier/ellipsoidal treatment of bounds; no regime-driven estimate or recovery path.

transferable: When generalizing a method to a wider problem class, show it reduces exactly to the established method on the special case (here LP) (abstract).

quotes.text: Our fundamental concept is to recast the idea of affine scaling and view it as the result of using an ellipsoidally shaped trust region on iterative subproblems.
The algorithm reduces to the primal barrier interior point method for linear programming problems.

title: Numerical Optimization Techniques
contribution: NSF award CCR-9400881 (1994-96) proposing a Newton/variable-metric hybrid for large non-sparse unconstrained problems from weather forecasting and two routes for inequality constraints in large NLP: an ellipsoidal method feeding equality-constrained subproblems to existing software, and a trust-region primal-dual extension related to SQP (abstract; CV p. 4).
problem_entry: Large unstructured non-sparse unconstrained problems (weather forecasting) and inequality constraints in large NLP (abstract).
key_idea: Combine Newton methods with variable metric updating; handle inequalities by an ellipsoidal-type method leading to equality-constrained subproblems for existing software, or by extending the LP primal-dual method within a trust-region framework tied to SQP (abstract).
experiments: Planned tests on a set of large problems, with careful treatment of ill-conditioning (abstract).
positioning: Grant record, not a publication; Sep 1994-Aug 1996, $109,998 (CV p. 4). Inferred from timing: route (ii) matches S191 and later S008/S009 (not verified).
limits_future: Outcomes not in the record.

method_links.note: Engine half: constraint handling designed so existing equality-constrained software can be reused.

quotes.text: This approach has the advantage of leading readily into a sequence of equality constrained subproblems which can be solved by existing software.
The algorithm is posed in the framework of trust region methods, and its relationship with sequential quadratic programming is fully exploited.

title: Nonlinear Optimization

problem_entry: Limited-memory economy not exploited for nonlinear constraints; nonconvex interior methods; NEOS lacks modelling-language interaction (abstract).
key_idea: Compact limited-memory representations so an iteration costs a fraction of standard SQP; trust-region framework for uniform treatment of convex and nonconvex cases; identify crucial ingredients (model, merit function, ill-conditioned subproblem solves) (abstract).

The research will be guided by a combination of numerical testing and convergence analysis.

title: Numerical optimization

By presenting the motivating ideas for each algorithm, we try to stimulate the reader’s intuition and make the technical details easier to follow.

contribution: NSF award ATM-0086579 (2001-03, with S. J. Wright and NCEP) proposing enriched limited-memory quasi-Newton methods, automatic CG preconditioners and structured quasi-Newton least-squares methods for 3D/4D-Var data assimilation, tested in existing assimilation codes with a theory of the effect of inaccuracies (abstract; CV p. 3).
problem_entry: Reduce computer time and increase reliability of 3D/4D data assimilation in meteorology (abstract).
key_idea: Enriched L-BFGS, automatic preconditioners for CG, structured quasi-Newton methods for nonlinear least squares, for background covariances without simple sparsity and robust to varying resolution (abstract).

title: Active-Set and Interior Algorithms for Non-Linear Optimization
contribution: NSF award 0514772 (2005) proposing an EQP active-set method (LP active-set guess, then EQP, with two quasi-independent trust regions) and a barrier-parameter rule that minimizes quality functions, with corrector steps and a globalization that interferes minimally with the adaptive choice (abstract).
problem_entry: Limitations of traditional SQP; controlling the barrier parameter in interior methods, 'one of the most difficult algorithmic questions' (abstract).
key_idea: LP to guess the active set, EQP for optimality, two trust regions acting quasi-independently; barrier parameter chosen each iteration by minimizing quality functions; globalization designed to interfere as little as possible (abstract).
positioning: Continues the LP/EQP line of S035 (2004) and leads to the adaptive-barrier study S029 (2009) (inferred from timing).
limits_future: Software for circuit simulation, computational chemistry, finance, PDE-based optimization and traffic equilibrium (abstract).

method_links.note: The safeguard is designed to leave the working adaptive heuristic intact rather than replace it.
The barrier-update choice, an open question, becomes a funded study (cf. S029).
Target: a procedure effective in practice and supported by global convergence guarantees.

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: two-phase active-set prediction, then an equality-constrained/subspace step
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: LP guess of the optimal active set, then an equality-constrained QP, with separate trust regions.

quotes.text: Research focuses on one of the most difficult algorithmic questions: how to design a procedure for controlling the barrier parameter that is effective in practice and is supported by global convergence guarantees.
A globalization procedure that interferes with adaptive choices of the barrier parameter as little as possible will be developed.

problem_entry: Large-scale NLP including large reduced spaces, where SQP's general QP per iteration does not scale (abstract).
key_idea: LP plus EQP subproblems that scale well; economical piecewise linear models conforming to the theoretical guidelines of [6] (abstract).
experiments: Comparison with SNOPT and Knitro/Active; results not read (abstract).

contribution: NSF award DMS-1216567 (2012-16) proposing dynamic-sample methods bridging stochastic and batch methods, provably convergent active-set methods building on primal-dual active-set and orthant-wise methods, and interior methods with infeasibility detection under a unified optimization/feasibility/transition theory (abstract).

The second goal is to develop a convergence theory that is applicable to both active set and interior point methods consisting of three components: an optimization phase, a feasibility phase, and a mechanism for transitioning between the two phases.

title: Second order methods for optimizing convex matrix functions and sparse covariance clustering
contribution: Argues against the premise that second-order information is too expensive for matrix optimization in machine learning, giving Hessian representations with proofs, second-order methods for l1-regularized Jeffreys divergence, and a speech-recognition model compression by more than 200x (abstract).
problem_entry: The received premise that second-order information is too expensive, so first-order iterations are likely optimal (abstract).

positioning: Continues the IBM second-order line of S043 (inferred from authors and topic).
limits_future: Not stated (abstract).

method_links.note: The field's premise is stated in its own terms and then contested.
Structure of matrix functions makes second-order information affordable.

transferable: Open a paper by stating the field's premise in one sentence and then the counter-claim the paper will support (abstract).
coauthors: GM Chin, PA Olsen, SJ Rennie

quotes.text: The premise for utilizing such algorithms is that second order information is too expensive to employ, and so simple first-order iterations are likely to be optimal.
In this paper, we argue that second-order information is in fact efficiently accessible in many matrix optimization problems, and can be effectively incorporated into optimization algorithms.
